hero.title: Experimental media systems spanning film, sound, computation, installation, and speculative fiction.
hero.lede: Tony Yanick is an artist, educator, and computational media researcher working across film/video, sound, installation, generative systems, and participatory media environments. His work investigates how technological infrastructures, speculative narratives, and audiovisual systems shape perception, collective desire, and lived experience through unstable relationships between image, signal, memory, and space.

works.title: Projects unfolding across film, sound, installation, computation, transmission, and speculative media environments.

statement.title: My work operates through fiction—not as representation, but as a force that produces conditions.
paragraphs: I am interested in how narrative, myth, mediated images, and technological systems organize collective desire, and how these structures persist, circulate, and mutate across media environments.

The work develops across film, sound, installation, performance, and computational media—not as movement between disciplines, but as interference between forms. Image, sound, code, archives, and spatial systems interact to produce unstable relationships between perception, atmosphere, participation, and interpretation.

Many works unfold through projected image, live signal routing, synthetic voice, tape-based processes, generative image systems, networked participation, or computational feedback structures. Installations are treated less as static objects than as evolving conditions in which viewers encounter fragments, delays, repetitions, and unstable narrative relations over time.

I return repeatedly to temporal displacement. Fragments of possible worlds appear out of sequence—past events reconfigured as future projections, speculative structures embedded within existing archives, signals that arrive too early or too late.
Computational systems extend this condition. I engage generative and networked media not simply as tools for production, but as infrastructures that compress, redistribute, and reorganize perception.
There is no stable image at the end of this process—only signals that continue to circulate.

research.title: Investigating computational media as operational environments rather than neutral tools.

cards.title: Limits of CTRL
cards.text: Limits of CTRL: Neural Bending and the Generic Machine investigates generative AI models as infrastructural cultural systems rather than image-generation tools. The research focuses on intervention, probabilistic behavior, recursion, operational constraints, and the relationship between synthetic media and collective perception.

cards.title: Neural bending
cards.text: Neural bending treats generative systems as mutable environments whose internal operations can be redirected through interference, recursion, constraint, feedback, and distributed procedural modification rather than prompt-based output extraction alone.

cards.title: Media environments
cards.text: The research examines how computational media reorganizes spectatorship, memory, labor, authorship, and perception through interfaces, datasets, network structures, synthetic imagery, and algorithmic distribution systems.

teaching.title: Teaching across systems rather than fixed disciplines.
teaching.intro: Courses combine moving image production, sound design, editing, installation practice, computational media, experimental publishing, and critical media theory through project-based collaborative learning environments. Students are encouraged to move fluidly between analog and digital processes while developing technical literacy, conceptual rigor, and sustainable creative workflows.

materials.title: Systems-based media studio
materials.text: A studio model that asks students to build relationships between image, sound, code, archive, installation, and spatial experience rather than treating media as separate disciplines.

materials.title: Computational media as environment
materials.text: Assignments introduce computational systems as cultural and perceptual infrastructures, foregrounding constraints, feedback, iteration, recursion, and critical technical literacy through hands-on experimentation.

materials.title: Analog / digital publication systems
materials.text: A hybrid print and screen sequence connecting risograph processes, archives, typography, sequencing, networked distribution, and experimental publishing workflows.

projects.title: HYPNAGNOSIS
projects.format: Risograph works, altered-state artifacts, print/media environment
projects.summary: An evolving body of risograph works, altered-state artifacts, and speculative print structures concerned with sleep paralysis, hypnagogic imagery, unstable embodiment, dream architecture, and perceptual drift.
projects.system: HYPNAGNOSIS approaches printmaking as a neurological and perceptual interface. Registration drift, repeated forms, grain accumulation, overprint behavior, degraded textures, and unstable figure construction operate as material evidence of bodies moving between waking and dream states. The project spans print editions, diagrammatic systems, publication experiments, installation configurations, and hybrid analog/digital image processes.
projects.embed: Image sequence / print documentation embed slot

projects.title: COSMOMORPHOSIS
projects.format: Generative audiovisual installation driven by ISS telemetry
projects.summary: A generative audiovisual installation in which orbital telemetry from the International Space Station modulates image, sound, duration, rhythm, and nonlinear temporal behavior.
projects.system: COSMOMORPHOSIS treats telemetry not as raw input but as an environmental condition shaping audiovisual emergence. Orbital position, movement, delay, and transmission irregularities reorganize the relationship between body, infrastructure, planetary scale, and machine perception. The installation evolves continuously through live data, procedural audiovisual transformation, and recursive temporal displacement.
projects.embed: Video / live telemetry environment embed slot

projects.title: TRANSMISSIONS
projects.format: Speculative transmission system, sound, voice, distributed media
projects.summary: An evolving broadcast-fiction environment combining spoken word, experimental hip-hop structures, pirate radio aesthetics, speculative fiction, distributed signal systems, and participatory media practices.
projects.system: TRANSMISSIONS operates through fragmented broadcasts, transmission drift, synthetic archives, unstable narrative accumulation, and collective signal contamination across sound, performance, print, and installation contexts.
projects.embed: Audio player / transmission archive embed slot

projects.title: SHAPE OF A PACKET
projects.summary: A participatory media installation built around mobile systems, localized connectivity, shared archives, participant contribution, and temporary communication infrastructures.
projects.system: The project makes network behavior materially and socially perceptible. Participants contribute images, recordings, messages, traces, and fragments into a temporary distributed archive assembled through local wireless systems and collaborative interaction. Rather than representing networks abstractly, the installation stages networked behavior as lived spatial and collective experience.
projects.embed: Local network interface / participatory archive embed slot

projects.title: N2: THE SECRETARY
projects.format: Language, archive, synthetic media, signal environment
projects.summary: A layered archive-fiction environment composed through language systems, synthetic image generation, degraded documentation, procedural voice, and unstable administrative structures.
projects.system: N2: THE SECRETARY organizes documents, recordings, transcripts, synthetic images, and procedural fragments into a speculative bureaucratic system whose authority remains unresolved. The work operates through incomplete evidence, recursive administrative language, signal contamination, and uncertain archival logic, blurring the relationship between fiction, memory, institutional procedure, and machine-generated media.
projects.embed: Archive reader / signal environment excerpt slot

projects.title: ARTIFICIAL CINEMA
projects.summary: A computational audiovisual environment treating AI and generative systems as operative cinematic conditions rather than output-generation tools.
projects.system: The project approaches model behavior as a mutable audiovisual environment shaped through recursive generation, prompt choreography, procedural constraints, synthetic archives, feedback systems, and temporal arrangement. Cinema becomes distributed across interfaces, datasets, machine perception, and live computational processes.
projects.embed: A/V excerpt / computational system capture embed slot

projects.title: VARIATION 79 / PODKOP
projects.summary: Experimental audiovisual works exploring repetition, recursion, mediated memory, signal residue, and altered temporal experience through image, rhythm, and sound.
projects.system: These works investigate recurrence as both structural and perceptual condition. Images, gestures, sounds, and fragments return altered through layering, delay, interruption, degradation, and recursive transformation. Rather than stable narrative progression, the works generate fields of accumulation, repetition, and unresolved temporal drift.
projects.embed: Audiovisual excerpt / screening documentation embed slot

projects.title: The Fixers: Naudia Loftis
projects.summary: A collaborative documentary centered on Naudia Loftis, a seventeen-year-old community organizer working within Cleveland’s Kinsman neighborhood during the 2016 Republican National Convention.
projects.system: Built through interviews, proximity, collaboration, and community participation, the film foregrounds lived experience within conditions shaped by systemic violence, displacement, and political instability. Rather than imposing external narrative authority, the work creates space for participants to articulate social and personal realities through dialogue, presence, and collective exchange.
projects.embed: Documentary excerpt / community screening documentation embed slot

projects.title: Make America Great Again ... And Again
projects.summary: An experimental video work and Short and Sweet Festival Outstanding Film award winner drawing on Octavia E. Butler’s Parable trilogy to examine political language, mediated desire, and speculative power.
projects.system: Through montage, abstraction, layered media fragments, and recursive slogan structures, the project investigates how political narratives circulate as systems of emotional management, identity construction, and social control. The work approaches speculative fiction not as distant allegory but as an active structure shaping contemporary political reality.
projects.embed: Experimental video excerpt / festival documentation embed slot

projects.title: surFACE
projects.format: Short film, analog recording systems, tape-based process
projects.summary: A short film developed within the larger TAPEHEADS project investigating analog recording systems, repetitive drawing practices, feedback, and the material instability of image and sound.
projects.system: Constructed through iterative drawing, recording, playback, degradation, layering, and analog transformation, the work treats marks as unstable audiovisual material rather than static representation. Faces, textures, distortions, and sound evolve together through recursive recording behavior and tape-based feedback structures.
projects.embed: Short film excerpt / analog system documentation embed slot

projects.title: Flow Lines (3-channel video)
projects.summary: A three-channel collaborative installation developed in response to Isaac Julien’s Kapital, exploring migration, geography, historical memory, and movement through the Niagara River region.
projects.system: The Niagara River functions simultaneously as landscape, infrastructural boundary, historical route, and temporal flow system connected to the Underground Railroad. Through layered moving image, environmental rhythm, spoken language, and multi-channel spatial arrangement, the work approaches landscape as a living structure through which histories are carried, transformed, and reinterpreted.
projects.embed: Three-channel video excerpt / installation documentation embed slot

projects.title: BOBBI LYNN
projects.summary: A music video exploring memory, grief, intimacy, and familial relationships through generative image systems and synthetic reconstruction.
projects.system: Centered on a son’s recollection of his relationship with his mother, the work replaces direct photographic reconstruction with unstable synthetic imagery generated through machine-learning systems. Memory becomes probabilistic, fragmented, and continuously reassembled through computational mediation, destabilizing distinctions between recollection, simulation, intimacy, and loss.
projects.embed: Music video excerpt / generative image documentation embed slot

projects.title: Dossier 37
projects.format: Audiovisual work, forensic interface, data visualization
projects.summary: An audiovisual work developed in collaboration with AUDINT investigating sonic warfare discourse, disinformation systems, geopolitical narrative production, and perceptual instability.
projects.system: Emerging from discourse surrounding alleged sonic attacks on US diplomatic personnel in Cuba and South China, the project examines how fear, rumor, signal interpretation, and geopolitical speculation circulate through contemporary media systems. Structured through forensic interface aesthetics, Twitter activity visualization, signal mapping, and speculative timelines, the work treats evidence itself as unstable audiovisual terrain.
